method: Before reading the unit we reread the u04 exemplar and its five review rounds (a1.1-u04.r1–r5), u03 r1 and r2, u01 r3 and SCHEMA §15. We read the files as they stood on disk. u03.json was last written 2026-09-28 00:34 UTC, after r2 (00:03). None of the files outside the unit that r2's open findings depend on has changed since r2: a1.1/lexicon.json and specs.json (23:03), a1.1/rule-cards.json (23:06), src/lib/lesson/check.js (19:40), src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (19:41), src/components/course-v2/ItemView.jsx (20:47), and the rules ALL-02, GRM-04, GRM-05, ITM-13, LEX-01, LEX-03 and LEX-07. Both reviewers read every German string of the current file: the title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (10 lines) and its gist item, the three inputs (30 lines) and Emre's chat post, both exam texts, the strategy card and the 8 redemittel. For Sp2 that covers situationDe, instructionsDe, the new openingLine, aiRole.personaDe, the cards, 8 hintWords and 10 model turns. For S2 it covers situationDe, taskDe, the 3 Leitpunkte and their cues, the checklist and the model text. We also read the 3 check lines, the story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine, promptDe, option and explanation.de, the 33 u03 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json and the two rule cards the unit shows. We solved all 88 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line only, permuted every tile set and tried every one-word correction. Every key is right. We ran 80 candidate learner answers through the player's own grader (checkItem.js → check.js) and read how ItemView resolves a TYPO. Because new answer types came back TYPO, we then scanned all 490 typed single-token items in every registered course. The scan built each key's person-ending twin (-st ↔ -t) and its possessive-person twins (m/d/s + ein-) and graded them with checkItem (F01). We counted the repair-bank items without errorTags across all courses (F04) and read grammar-spine.json for the errorTags each spine point declares. The exam block was checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json. l1 has 5 × richtig_falsch, 2 options, and two texts of 69 and 73 words in [56, 92]. sp2 has cards-ask, 2 rounds and 0 minutes' preparation, with real questions on each topic word (the u04 r3-F04 class). s2 has 3 distinct Leitpunkte, about 30 words, and Anrede and Gruß are not Leitpunkte. We also checked it against the rubrics sd1-sp2 (frage 2/1/0 and antwort 1/0.5/0 per turn) and sd1-s2, and against the Leitpunkt cue check in WritingTaskView.jsx l. 25–28 (lowercase substring, so „Lehrerin“ meets the cue „Lehrer“). We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (compile.mjs a1.1 --out/--banks-out: 12 units compiled) and read the bank entries a11-u03-s (with the new openingLine) and a11-u03-w. Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: t1 69, t2 73, chat 50, S2 model 29 (23 without Anrede and Gruß), Sp2 situation 45, cliffhanger 20, and inputs of 134, 130 and 139 words. The grammar ceiling was read against grammar-spine.json and curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U3. The load was read against level-profiles.json: 33 new entries, 15 of them productive (45.5 %). Can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json. The cast was read against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ages, origins, languages, residence, du/Sie relations). The story was read against u02, u04, u05, u07 and u08, and specs.json's u03 entry against the unit's spec. No 360 px walkthrough was run; that is the walkthrough reviewer's remit.

verdict: Not exit-ready. The unit's authors did everything r2 asked of u03.json. Both unit-owned minors are fixed cleanly: ls3-p11 now quotes Emre's line, and Nora's greeting is its own turn. The German is correct and idiomatic on every model surface, all 88 keys are right, all five can-dos are performed, the exam block is exact to sd1.json, and the validator is green. What stops exit is still held outside the unit file, and nothing outside it has moved since r2: no checker, lexicon, rule-card or rail file has changed. (1) F01, MAJOR, stop-the-line, and wider than r2 measured. The grader forgives both of this unit's new grammar points as spelling slips. This is not only the unchanged stem vowel r2 found. check.js endingDiffers compares only the last letter, so the person ending -st/-t is a typo: „schläfst“ for „Es ___ schon.“ in the scored c03, and „spricht“ for „Arjun, ___ du Englisch?“. The v2 topic „g.possessiv-mein-dein“ also misses STRICT_TOPIC's English „possessive“, so the mein/dein person swap is a typo too: „deine“ in c01, and „Ist das meine Mutter?“ in the scored correction c07. After one retry ItemView counts every typo as correct. So three of the eight scored Check items accept the error their grammar point exists to remove. Course-wide, the person-ending swap passes on 45 typed items in nine A1.1 units, seven of them Check items. One of those is u01's own Personalendung check („Woher kommt du?“ → typo). r2's proposed stem-vowel fix would close none of this; the fix belongs in the v2 checker wrapper, with a rail that grades each item's known wrong forms. (2) F02, MAJOR: the u03 word card for Partner still moves Sophie to Dresden with a partner, and its neighbours show the ihr-possessive (third round). (3) F03, MAJOR: lesen and schlafen, which carry the unit's productive Vokalwechsel drill, are still receptive (third round). Seven minors are logged. Three are small unit edits: tag the Vokalwechsel items with the errorTag the spine already declares (F04), pay off u02's „Anmeldung: Arjun Nair“ hook with „Noch nicht“ (F06), and swap the one Check tile the learner has never seen, „abends“ (F07). Four are owner-held carry-overs: the checker's sentence-wide caseSensitive (F05), the rule cards (F08), detector noise (F09) and the formal Befinden phrase in the lexicon (F10).

findings.problem: This is r2-F01, still open: none of the three checker files has changed since before r2. It is also wider than r2 measured. r2 found the unchanged stem vowel („schlaft“, „lest“, „sprechst“). Two more error types come back TYPO, and both are errors this unit exists to remove. (1) The person ending. endingDiffers treats a word as a different ending only when its last letter changes. The person endings -st and -t differ in the second-to-last letter, so a person error is a typo. „schläfst“ in „Das Kind ist müde. Es ___ schon.“ (c03, the scored Check), „spricht“ in „Arjun, ___ du Englisch?“ (ls2-p01) and „Er sprichst gut Deutsch.“ (ls2-p10) all pass after one retry. (2) The possessive person. STRICT_TOPIC was written for the live course's English topic names. The v2 id „g.possessiv-mein-dein“ lacks the „e“ of „possessive“, so possessive gaps get the one-letter allowance. A mein/dein/sein swap keeps the last letter. So „deine“ for „meine“ (c01) is a typo. In the error corrections the learner types the whole sentence, and „Ist das meine Mutter?“ for „Ist das dein Mutter?“ (c07, the scored Check) is a typo as well. That answer fixes the ending but changes the person, which is exactly the mein/dein distinction that ls1-s03, ls3-s01 and ls3-s03 teach. r2 said the possessive items are safe because their error changes the last letter. That holds only for mein → meine. ItemView counts every typo as correct after one retry, with errorTag null. On this unit, then, three of the eight scored Check items (c01, c03, c07) and the typed drill of both new spine points accept the target error, and the misses reach no repair pool. The course-wide scan tried every key's person-ending twin on the 490 typed single-token items in all registered courses. The twin grades typo on 50 real verb forms. 45 of them are in nine A1.1 units: u01 9, u02 3, u03 5, u04 2, u07 10, u08 3, u09 4, u10 8, u12 1. Seven are scored Check items: a1.1-u01-c02 („Woher kommt du?“), u02-c02 („Wohnt du in Leipzig?“), u03-c03, u07-c01, u09-c02, u10-c01 and u10-c03. The other five are in a2.2-u04, b1.1-u04 and b2.2-u04. So u01's own spine point, the Personalendung of g.praesens, is not assessed by u01's Check either. The possessive-person swap grades typo on nine items: u03 ×6 and u06 ×3 (meinen/deinen/seinen). r2's proposed fix, a strict rule for stem-vowel items plus an unchanged-sentence rule, would close neither new type. Under §9.4 the class is stop-the-line: it is in nine A1.1 units and has no rule. It is rated MAJOR as a gate hole.
findings.fix: Checker owner, with tests. CLAUDE.md: the rule belongs in the checker, never in a widened or narrowed accepted list. Fix it in the v2 wrapper so the live course's grading is untouched. (1) checkItem.js: pass strict: true when the item's topic is a v2 spine id (/^g\./) and its key is one token. normalizeAnswer still folds ae/oe/ue and ss, so „schlaeft“ stays correct, and a case-only slip stays a typo. (2) Apply a v2 ending test in checkItem.js, or change endingDiffers itself if the live course owner agrees: an edit within the last two letters of a word is an ending change, never a typo. Then „Woher kommt du?“ is WRONG inside a sentence answer too. (3) error_correction: an answer equal to its own quoted sentence after normalisation is WRONG. The token or tokens in which the quoted sentence and the key differ are compared strictly, so „Ist das meine Mutter?“ is WRONG. (4) SCHEMA owner: add the verb-ending ErrorTag (u01 r3 F10). Unit: no edit for this finding; the tag edit is F04. Do not turn the typed items into choice items to route around the checker; that would break the pool's recall share (ITM-06).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-13, or a new ITM rail: for every typed item with a g.* topic, generate the item's known wrong forms and grade each with the player's checkItem. Each must come back WRONG. The forms are: (a) the quoted sentence of an error_correction; (b) the person-ending twin of a finite-verb key (-st ↔ -t, -e ↔ -en) when the twin is a real form of the lemma (lexicon verb_forms or lib-validate/strong-verbs.mjs); (c) the unchanged stem vowel of a Vokalwechsel key; (d) the m/d/s swap of a possessive key; (e) in an error_correction, the target token replaced by another person's form. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u01-c02 („kommt“), a1.1-u03-c03 („schlaft“, „schläfst“), a1.1-u03-c07 („Ist das meine Mutter?“) and a1.1-u03-ls2-p10 (the unchanged sentence). Passing fixture: a1.1-u03-ls1-p01 „mein“ → wrong. The test runs over all registered courses. Today it fails on the 50 person-ending items, the 9 possessive items and r2's stem-vowel and unchanged-sentence lists.
